title: Backchannel
description: Short acknowledgements (haan, hmm, achha, ok) said while the agent holds the floor are the caller listening, not taking the turn. A local VAD still stops the agent's audio as soon as anyone talks over it, so real barge-in stays fast; an utterance made only of phrases on this list is then dropped before it becomes a turn or reaches chat history, and the agent's paused reply resumes after interruption.falseInterruptionTimeoutMs. Said over the end of a question it is the caller's answer instead (answerWithinMs). The words of every language are used together, because people in one call mix languages and a recognizer does not always transcribe in the session language's script.

maxWords.description: The longest utterance still heard as an acknowledgement. Anything longer is a turn, whatever its words.

answerWithinMs.description: An acknowledgement said over a reply that ends in a question answers it and becomes the caller's turn, when that reply then plays to its end within this long of the caller falling silent and the caller says nothing more. Said earlier, over the rest of the reply, it was the caller listening and is dropped; said over a statement, it is always dropped.

words.description: The acknowledgements, and the affirmatives of the interruption lexicon: an affirmative said alone holds the agent's reply, an affirmative followed by more speech yields it.

negatives.description: Phrases (no, wait, ruko, नहीं) that yield the agent's reply wherever they fall in an utterance, below interruption.minWords. An utterance holding one is never an acknowledgement. The negatives of every language are used together.

reviewed.description: Whether a native speaker has checked a language's words and negatives, keyed by base language. Metadata only; it changes no behaviour.
